area: Roman numerals in safe contexts: monarchs, popes and family suffixes (ordinal, 'the Eighth'), world wars, events and sequels, document parts and classifications (cardinal, 'four'), Roman-numeral years, and Jr./Sr. A Roman reader already ships: it came in with FIN-877 (commit 52f33ff, NEW-R5) and is in the current b06b926 build. So these rules rework that reader rather than add a new one. Everything else stays spelled, and a lone 'I' stays a pronoun unless a narrow, keyword-specific gate passes.

rules.name: R0. Rework the FIN-877 reader rather than add a second pass
rules.where: TextNormalizer.readRomanNumerals and readRoman, added in 52f33ff (FIN-877 NEW-R5) and present in the b06b926 build. Move the call out of TextNormalizer.normalize, which runs after unshout, to Phonemizer.phonemize right after custom.mark and before unshout, only when normalizes is on. Replace readRoman's decision logic with R1-R14: the numeralNouns list, the pronounFollowers blocklist and the 'any capitalised word + numeral = cardinal' fallback.
rules.trigger: Shared mechanics. (1) A candidate is a canonical numeral `^M{0,3}(CM|CD|D?C{0,3})(XC|XL|L?X{0,3})(IX|IV|V?I{0,3})$`, non-empty, all one case, with no letter or digit on either side. A following hyphen, possessive or punctuation mark is fine. Today's romanCandidate sees only upper-case I, V, X and L; extend it to lower case (R4, R5) and to C, D and M (R4 with four or more letters, R11). (2) Work on the plain stretches between custom-lexicon marks. When looking back for a trigger, a mark counts as its label, as in readArrows. Unwrap and convert a mark only when its label is X (exact) or vi (case-sensitive) and a trigger comes right before it. Never rewrite any other mark. (3) Write words from NumberWords, never digits. Cardinals go in lower case; ordinals in title case ('the Eighth'). Hyphenate compound tens ('fifty-eight'). Write 'oh five' as two words. Hundreds take no 'and' in US and keep it in GB. Inside a shouted sentence, write every inserted word in capitals. (4) Keep the trigger as written, except that Ch., Vol. and Mk (including glued 'MkIV') expand to Chapter, Volume and Mark before a numeral. (5) Order: R11, R1, R5, R2 with R3, R4 with R6 and R7, R8a, R10, R8b, R9, R12.
rules.reads_as: Nothing by itself. It sets scope, order and output format.
rules.risks: The FIN-877 reader is live and misreads 24 of the 85 frozen sentences today: the pronoun I after Part, Super Bowl, Terminal, Mark, Type, Series, Form and titled names; single V and L after given names and after Gen, Lot and Section; IV after drug names and Pt; Subaru XV; St. Thomas VI. Keeping its catch-all next to the new rules keeps those errors. Digits as output would hit the fraction and range rules ('Phase 1/2' already reads 'one half') and fail the harness's spacing comparison. Running before custom.mark would break lexicon keys that contain numerals: SOC 2 Type II, MiFID II, Basel III, GTA V, Grand Theft Auto VI, Atlas V, Peak XV, RISC-V, Mac OS X, Model X, Xbox Series X.

rules.name: R1. World wars
rules.where: TextNormalizer Roman pass (today: the WW rule in TextNormalizer.rules plus readRoman's 'world war' branch)
rules.trigger: (a) Glued and case-sensitive: `(?<![\p{L}\p{N}])WW(III|II|I|3|2|1)(?![\p{L}\p{N}])`. A space or hyphen is allowed only before II or III ('WW II', 'WW-II'). It is never allowed before an Arabic digit ('I joined WW 2 years ago' is WeightWatchers) or before a lone I ('WW I think'). (b) 'World War' in title case or ALL CAPS, one space, then I, II or III with no letter or digit after it. This always converts, with no pronoun check. Two exceptions apply to a single I. After lower-case 'world war', the I must pass the I-gate ('A third world war I fear'). After 'the World War', it converts only before punctuation or a word from a WWI list: memorial, era, centenary, centennial, armistice, generation, veteran(s), poet(s), poetry, trenches, years, soldier(s), museum, battlefield(s), cemetery, monument, history. That keeps 1920s prose ('During the World War I served in France') as the pronoun.
rules.reads_as: 'World War One', 'World War Two', 'World War Three'. 'WWII's' becomes 'World War Two's'; 'post-WWII' becomes 'post-World War Two'.
rules.risks: Today 'World War I was a disaster' reads 'eye' because 'was' is on the pronoun-follower list, and WWIII is spelled out. The drafted 'the World War I' exception, which sent the next word through the general I-gate noun list, would have regressed 'The World War I centenary', which is right today. WWDC is a lexicon mark and never matches.

rules.name: R2. People: monarchs, popes and family suffixes (ordinal)
rules.where: TextNormalizer Roman pass; name lists as static sets (today: regnalNames and regnalTitles)
rules.trigger: A, title. After King, Queen, Pope, Emperor, Empress, Tsar, Czar, Tsarina, Kaiser, Sultan, Pharaoh or Shah, any 1 to 3 capitalised name tokens, then the numeral. After Prince, Princess, Duke, Duchess, Grand Duke, Archduke, Saint or St., the name must be on the B list ('Duke Nukem II' is a game). B, bare listed name: the drafted list, with an optional 'the' in between ('Henry the VIII'). C, family suffix: a given name from a curated list, then 1 or 2 capitalised tokens or initials, then II, III or IV. Use the SSA top-1000 names minus those that are also ordinary English words (Major, King, Prince, Duke, Royal, Hunter, Chase, Mark, Will). C does not apply when the token before the numeral is an R4 keyword ('Lincoln Mark VII') or the phrase is on the R8a list. Numerals: upper case, value 2 to 39, two or more letters. Never XX or XXX after a name, because those are kisses ('Love, Mary XX'). Never IV before a clinical noun (fluids, antibiotics, access, line, drip, push, iron, contrast, dose: 'give John IV fluids'). Never VI after St. Thomas, St. John or St. Croix (the US Virgin Islands postal code). Single letters: V or X only when followed by a lower-case word, 'of', 's or ’s, a comma, or sentence-final punctuation. X is also never accepted at the end of the text or a line after a bare name ('Love, Mary X'), and never after Malcolm. A single letter followed by a capitalised word, with or without a period, is a middle initial ('Henry V. Poor', 'John L Smith', 'Mary V Jones'). The exception is after a regnal title, where '. ' + capital ends the sentence ('Queen Elizabeth I. It hangs…'). L, C, D and M are never numerals alone ('Henry L. Stimson'). A single I only through the I-gate (R13), and the gate applies after titles too.
rules.reads_as: 'the' + NumberWords.ordinal in title case: 'Henry the Eighth', 'Pope John the Twenty-third', 'Thurston Howell the Third', 'Elizabeth the First's'. An existing 'the' is not doubled.
rules.risks: Fixes misreadings live today: middle initials read as ordinals (5 frozen cases); a pronoun I after a titled name read as 'the first' (2); 'Duke Nukem the Second'; 'Saint Thomas the Sixth'; 'John the fourth fluids'; family suffixes after unlisted given names read as cardinals ('Howell three', 'King three', 'Rockefeller four'). Accepted misses: 'Charles I was beheaded', 'Charles X Gustav', obscure monarchs who aren't on the list, 'Mary Poppins II'.

rules.name: R3. Jr. and Sr. after a name
rules.where: TextNormalizer Roman pass, or the abbreviations section of TextNormalizer.rules
rules.trigger: As drafted. 'Jr.', 'Jr', 'Sr.' or 'Sr' right after a capitalised surname. The surname ends a name of two or more capitalised tokens, or is a single surname not followed by a capitalised word. Never at the start of a sentence, and never after a greeting or title word (Dear, Hi, Hello, Thanks, Sister, Mother).
rules.reads_as: 'Junior' or 'Senior', for both 'Jr.' and 'Jr', so the British voice says ʤˈuːnɪə like 'Junior' does. Keep the period only at the end of the text or line, or before a capitalised word.
rules.risks: Today 'Sr.' reads 'S R', and the GB gold entries for both 'Jr.' and 'Jr' give ʤˈuːnjə, so the GB voice fails both Jr cases. 'Sr. Mary' (Sister) belongs to the titles area.

rules.name: R4. Keywords before a numeral: document parts, classifications, events (cardinal)
rules.trigger: A keyword, then one space or no-break space, then a numeral. Mk can also be glued to it ('MkII', 'MkIV'). Document keywords: Chapter(s), Ch., Part(s), Book(s), Volume(s), Vol., Canto(s), Title(s), Article(s), Section(s), Schedule(s), Annex, Appendix (numerals of two or more letters only), Table(s), Plate, Psalm(s), Amendment, Episode(s), Act(s), Scene(s), page(s), Unit, Lesson, Module. Class keywords: Phase(s), Type(s), Stage(s), Class(es), Level(s), Grade(s), Tier(s), Category, Division, Factor. Event keywords: Super Bowl, Vatican, Apollo, Mark, Mk, Mk. Drop Pt./Pt, because in clinical notes it means patient ('Pt IV access'). Gen, Generation, Version, Model, Series, Form, Lot, Terminal, Step, Room, Gate, Track, Round, Group, Number, Year and the rest of today's extra numeralNouns are not keywords. Numerals: (1) Upper case with two or more letters: 2 to 89 if made only of I, V, X and L; a numeral containing C, D or M needs four or more letters. (2) A single V only after a title-case or ALL CAPS keyword, and not after Mark, Mk or Appendix ('class V extends Base' stays). (3) A single X only after a title-case or ALL CAPS Chapter, Part, Book, Volume, Title, Article, Canto, Psalm, Super Bowl or Apollo. (4) A single I only after a title-case or ALL CAPS keyword, and only if the I-gate passes. (5) C, D, L and M alone: never ('Section L', 'Lot L', 'Appendix C'). (6) Lower case as drafted. After document keywords: i, v and x numerals up to 39 with two or more letters, plus a single v. After class keywords: only ii, iii and iv. After event keywords: never. (7) Grade + numeral + '*' reads '… star'.
rules.reads_as: The keyword with abbreviations expanded, then the cardinal: 'Chapter four', 'Mark four', 'Factor eight', 'Factor five Leiden', 'Grade two star', 'Title four-E'. For 100 and up, US 'one hundred thirty-five' and GB 'one hundred and thirty-five'.
rules.risks: Fixes misreadings live today: 'Super Bowl one cried', 'Part one Played', 'Terminal one typed', 'Mark one disagree', 'Type one to', 'Series one', 'Form one nine', 'Gen five', 'Lot fifty', 'Section fifty', 'Pt four'. Accepted: 'Super Bowl I was played in 1967' stays 'eye', and 'Mark I tank' is missed.

rules.name: R5. Act and Scene citations
rules.trigger: As drafted: `(Act|ACT|act)\s+N(,|\.)?\s+(Scene|SCENE|scene|Sc\.|sc\.)\s+n`, where both numerals may be upper or lower case, including I and i.
rules.reads_as: 'Act one, Scene one', 'Act two, Scene two'.
rules.risks: This is the only place a lone lower-case i becomes 'one'. The whole citation has to match.

rules.name: R6. Lists and ranges after a converted numeral
rules.where: TextNormalizer Roman pass (part of R2, R4 and R8)
rules.trigger: After a numeral that was just converted, keep going while the separator is ', ', ' and ', ' or ', ', and ', ' & ', ' to ', ' through ', '–', '-' or '/' and a Roman numeral of the same case follows. An Arabic digit never continues the run ('Form I-9', 'I-95'). In a continuation, a single V or X counts, a single I must pass the I-gate, and C, D, L or M alone never counts. A pronoun after 'and' is not a continuation ('Chapter IV and I loved it').
rules.reads_as: '–' and '-' become ' to ' ('Parts two to four'); '/' joins with a hyphen ('Phase one-two'); word separators stay as written ('Types one and two').
rules.risks: Low. The output is words, so the fraction rule never sees 'I/II'.

rules.name: R7. Sub-stage letters
rules.trigger: As drafted: after Stage, Phase, Type, Class or Grade, a numeral from I to IV with one letter a, b, c, A, B or C attached ('IIIA', 'IIb'). Also after a hyphen ('Title IV-E', 'Class I-A').
rules.reads_as: Cardinal, a hyphen, then the letter in capitals: 'Stage three-A', 'Class two-B', 'Title four-E'.
rules.risks: Low. A glued 'Ia' is never the pronoun.

rules.name: R8. Sequels and titles: a curated list plus a narrow general rule (cardinal)
rules.trigger: R8a, curated. Needed for IV, XI, XV, single V or X, and values over 39: Rocky, Rambo, Creed, Superman, Godfather, Star Trek, Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, Kingdom Hearts, Street Fighter, Mortal Kombat, Diablo, Warcraft, StarCraft, Civilization, Age of Empires, Hearts of Iron, Europa Universalis, Crusader Kings, Dark Souls, Baldur's Gate, Elder Scrolls, Hades, Doom, Quake, Halloween, Psycho, Saturn (V only), WrestleMania (up to LXXXIX). R8b, general. A title-case word followed by an upper-case II, III, VI, VII, VIII, IX or XII to XXXIX. The word must not be a sentence starter, a hyphenated word, a listed given name or a keyword. Never IV, XI, XV, XX, XXX, XL, LI, LV, LX, LIV or a single letter.
rules.reads_as: 'Rocky three', 'Frozen two', 'Major League two', 'Final Fantasy ten', 'WrestleMania forty'.
rules.risks: Today's catch-all reads any capitalised word + numeral as a number. That gets Frozen II, Major League II, Factor VIII and England XV right, but also gives 'Ceftriaxone four', 'Zofran four for', 'Subaru fifteen' and 'fifty-four Golf'. A curated-only R8, as drafted, would lose the good readings; R8b keeps them and drops the bad ones. Residual risk: an unlisted capitalised brand + II/III/VI-XXXIX that isn't a sequel. None common found.

rules.name: R9. Numeral before a colon subtitle (cardinal)
rules.where: TextNormalizer Roman pass (after R2 and R8)
rules.trigger: As drafted (title-case word + I/V/X numeral of two or more letters from 2 to 39, excluding IV, or a single V, then ':'). Most of these cases are now covered by R8b, so R9 only adds the single V.
rules.reads_as: 'Star Trek two: The Wrath of Khan', 'Elder Scrolls five: Skyrim'.
rules.risks: IV stays excluded ('Vancomycin IV: 1 g'). Lowest value here; it can ship later.

rules.name: R10. Team XI and XV (cardinal)
rules.trigger: XI as drafted: after a title-case word that isn't a monarch trigger, or after starting, first, second, third, playing, best or combined. Not before 'Jinping', and never after an ALL CAPS word. XV only after a rugby side from a short list (England, Scotland, Wales, Ireland, France, Italy, Lions, Barbarians) or after starting, unchanged or matchday.
rules.reads_as: 'the England eleven', 'the starting eleven', 'the England fifteen'.
rules.risks: 'Subaru XV' isn't a rugby side, so it stays spelled. 'England XV' is right today only through the catch-all, so without this extension it regresses.

rules.name: R11. Years in Roman numerals
rules.trigger: As drafted: a standalone upper-case canonical numeral of four or more letters with a value from 1000 to 2099. A '©' may come before it and punctuation after it. Use the strict canonical pattern ('MCMC' is not a numeral), and require the 1000-2099 window ('DCCC' is 800).
rules.reads_as: NumberWords.year with the spacing the stack uses: 'nineteen eighty-four', 'seventeen seventy-six', 'nineteen oh five' (two words, not num2words' 'oh-five'). 2000-2009: US 'two thousand six', GB 'two thousand and six'.
rules.risks: No canonical numeral of four or more letters is a word or a lexicon key. The output's spacing must match the says side, or the harness fails it.

rules.name: R12. A heading line that is only a numeral
rules.trigger: As drafted (`^[ \t]*(N)[.:]?[ \t]*$`, where N uses I, V and X only, two or more letters, value 2 to 39), excluding IV, XI, XX and XXX.
rules.risks: A lone 'IV' line in a medication table ('Route:\nIV') and 'XX' kisses on their own line would otherwise read 'Four' and 'Twenty'. A lone 'I.' line stays 'eye'.

rules.name: R13. The I-gate (when a lone I can be a numeral)
rules.where: TextNormalizer helper used by R1, R2, R4 and R6
rules.trigger: A standalone upper-case I, already right after a trigger, is a numeral only if what follows it is one of these: (1) Punctuation or structure: end of text or line; , ; : ) ] ! ?; '.' (but after a bare name, '. ' + a capitalised word is a middle initial; after a regnal title it ends the sentence); 's or ’s; ' of '; ' ('; a spaced ' – ' or ' — '; '/', '-' or '–' + a Roman numeral (never an Arabic digit); ' and ', ' or ', ' & ', ' to ' or ' through ' + a Roman numeral. (2) A third-person verb, which the pronoun can't take: shows, lists, covers, describes, summarizes, summarises, presents, contains, includes, gives, explains, introduces, outlines, compares, reports, provides, establishes, begins, ends, deals, focuses, discusses, examines, defines. (3) A follower word for that keyword. Phase: trial(s), study, studies, clinical. Type: diabetes, diabetic, error(s), collagen, hypersensitivity, supernova(e). Stage: cancer, disease, tumor, tumour, breast, lung, colon, colorectal, prostate, ovarian, cervical, skin, melanoma, lymphoma, hypertension. Class: recall(s), device(s), obesity. Level: trauma, certification. Grade: listed. Schedule: drug(s), substance(s), narcotic(s). Title: funding, funds, school(s), program(s). Division: school(s), college(s), athlete(s), football, basketball, program(s), team(s). The keyword or name before the I must be in title case or ALL CAPS. With no trigger, I is never a numeral.
rules.risks: The drafted gate used one noun list for every keyword and blocked '. Capital' after any name. That would have regressed six readings that are right today: Schedule I drug, Level I trauma center, Stage I breast cancer, Class I recall, Table I shows, and 'Queen Elizabeth I. It…'. Keyword-specific followers keep those without opening the pronoun cases ('In Table I listed…' stays a pronoun, because 'listed' is allowed only after Grade). Accepted misses: 'Charles I was beheaded', 'Part I begins', 'Super Bowl I was played'.

rules.name: R14. Don't lower-case untriggered numerals in shouted text
rules.trigger: As drafted: return false for a canonical Roman numeral of two or more letters whose lower-case form isn't a gold word.
rules.reads_as: A numeral in a shouted sentence with no trigger is spelled letter by letter, as in mixed-case text. Today 'CHAPTER XVIII' reads ɛksvˈii and 'COPYRIGHT MCMLXXXIV' reads məkmlksɪv.
rules.risks: None found. MIX and DIV are gold words and still lower-case; CIVIL, LIVID, VIVID and DIM are not numerals.

open_questions: 1. A lone 'I' as a number. Recommend yes, gated, but with keyword-specific followers (R13) rather than one noun list. Today's reader already reads I as 'one' after any title-case keyword unless a verb from a short list follows. That gives correct readings ('Schedule I drug', 'Table I shows') and also the misreadings in the frozen set ('Super Bowl I cried', 'Mark I disagree', 'Terminal I typed', 'Form I-9', 'Series I bonds'). The gate here keeps the first group and drops the second.

2. Roman-numeral years with no context ('Copyright MCMLXXXIV', '© MMXXIV', a foundation stone reading 'MCMV'). Recommend yes, for four or more letters between 1000 and 2099. Decide the British form for 2000-2009: natural British speech says 'two thousand and six', but the stack reads the digits '2006' without the 'and' in both voices. The set expects the 'and' for GB; drop that says_gb if you want Roman and Arabic years to match.

3. Sequels (changed recommendation). The draft proposed a curated list only, which would REGRESS readings that are right today ('Frozen two', 'Major League two', 'Factor eight', 'England fifteen'). Recommend a curated list for the risky numerals (IV, XI, XV, single letters, values over 39) plus a narrow general rule for II, III, VI-IX and XII-XXXIX after a title-case word (R8b). That still blocks 'Ceftriaxone four', 'Subaru fifteen' and 'fifty-four Golf'.

4. Lower-case list markers '(i)', '(ii)' in legal text. Recommend: not in Core for now. Note that '(ii)' currently reads 'ee' (ˈii), which is wrong. I didn't freeze it, so a Law pack or a later Core rule can change it freely.

5. Team numbers. Recommend 'eleven' for XI as drafted, and 'fifteen' for XV only after a rugby side from a short list (England, Scotland, Wales, Ireland, France, Italy, Lions). Without that, 'The England XV', which is right today, regresses when XV leaves the general rule.

6. A line that is only a numeral ('XIV.'). Recommend yes for II to XXXIX, excluding IV, XI, XX and XXX: a lone 'IV' line appears in medication tables, and 'XX' on its own line is a sign-off of kisses.

7. New: 'the World War I' in 1920s prose ('During the World War I served in France') against modern 'the World War I centenary/generation/armistice'. Recommend converting after 'the World War' only before punctuation or a WWI noun list (R1), so old prose keeps the pronoun. Alternatively, always convert, and accept that the rare archaic sentence reads 'one'.

8. New: 'LIV Golf' needs a lexicon entry for 'liv'. The Roman rules can only stop it reading 'fifty-four'. Should the speech case stay (it fails until someone adds the entry), or move to the tech or sports lexicon's tests?
review_notes: The draft's premise is out of date. A Roman reader already ships: it came in with FIN-877 (commit 52f33ff, NEW-R5, merged into this branch) and is in the current build (.build/release rebuilt at b06b926, after the draft was captured on 1070ec4). On today's build, 69 of the 115 speech cases pass in both voices (140 of 230 voice runs).
